1. Overview & Motivation
In animation engines, audio requirements are fundamentally distinct from game engines or static media players:

items: **Discrete & Scrubbable Time**: Animation timelines are non-linear, reversible, scrubbable, and time-scaled (`scene.time`, `scene.seekTo()`, `scene.timeScale`, `scene.pause()`), whereas the browser's hardware `AudioContext.currentTime` runs unconditionally forward in real-time seconds.
**Animation Choreography**: Voiceover speech dictates animation pacing, sound effects trigger on animation milestones, and background music must automatically duck when narration occurs.
**WebGPU Reactivity**: Audio frequencies and waveforms must stream directly to GPU uniform buffers and 1D spectrum textures for real-time shaders without costly CPU readback bottlenecks.

**Synchronized Video Export**: High-fidelity video rendering requires frame-synchronized audio muxing into MP4 and WebM files directly in the browser ([Recorder.ts](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/recorder/Recorder.ts)).
**Zero Core Bloat**: Mathematical, 3D, and shader scenes that do not require audio must remain 100% tree-shakeable with zero runtime overhead or premature `AudioContext` instantiation.

blocks.text: Retiam implements a **Hybrid Plugin Architecture**: the core engine ([Scene.ts](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Scene.ts)) provides a lightweight, generic event contract, while the entire audio graph, timeline tracking, decoders, spatial audio components, and analyzers live modularly in `src/engine/audio/`.

blocks.text: 2. Core Architectural Principles
A. Deterministic Timeline Synchronization (AudioTimeline.ts)
Web Audio's `AudioBufferSourceNode` is a single-use node: once stopped, it cannot be resumed. `AudioTimeline` abstracts this by managing a virtual timeline registry:

items: **Clip Scheduling**: Clips register `{ buffer, startTimeMs, durationMs, loop, volume, pitch }`.

children: Any currently playing buffer sources are stopped with a 4ms micro-ramp to eliminate audible waveform DC-offset clicks and pops.
The timeline identifies which clips overlap with `targetTimeMs` and computes the exact sub-buffer offset:

items: New `AudioBufferSourceNode` instances are spawned with `source.start(0, offsetSeconds)` and a 4ms micro-fade attack.
**Dynamic Time Scaling**: When `scene.timeScale` changes (e.g. slow-motion or fast-forward), active sources immediately adjust their playback rate:

blocks.text: B. Browser Autoplay Compliance & Auto-Resync (AudioPlugin.ts)
Browsers strictly enforce autoplay policies: `AudioContext` is created in `'suspended'` state and outputs console warnings if `source.start()` or `context.resume()` is called without a user gesture.
Retiam solves this with a **zero-warning deferred startup**:

items: **Deferred Playback**: If `this.context.state === 'suspended'`, `AudioTimeline` registers clip metadata but defers calling `source.start()`, producing zero console warnings.

**Comprehensive Auto-Unlock**: `AudioPlugin` attaches passive capture listeners (`pointerdown`, `touchstart`, `mousedown`, `keydown`, `click`) to the canvas, window, and parent iframe (when running inside Retiam Studio).

**Frame-Accurate Resync**: A `statechange` listener detects when the context becomes `'running'`. It immediately executes `timeline.seekTo(scene.time)`, beginning playback in exact frame-accurate synchronization with the running animation.

blocks.text: C. Multi-Bus Mixing & Master Dynamics Limiter (AudioManager.ts)
To eliminate digital clipping when multiple loud animations trigger sound effects simultaneously, the mixer graph routes through dedicated sub-busses:

items: **`BGM Bus`**: Dedicated to continuous music loops with independent volume, fade-ins, and fade-outs.
**`SFX Bus`**: Polyphonic one-shots triggered by animations or collisions.
**`Voiceover Bus`**: Speech tracks that automatically duck the BGM bus by a configurable ratio (default 75%) and smoothly restore it when speech completes.
**`DynamicsCompressorNode`**: A master brickwall limiter ($\text{threshold} = -3.0\text{dB}$, $\text{knee} = 12\text{dB}$, $\text{ratio} = 8:1$) ensuring studio-grade loudness without distortion.

blocks.text: D. 3D Spatial Audio & Camera Listener ECS

items: **[`AudioListenerComponent`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/audio/components/AudioListenerComponent.ts)**: Extends `Component` and attaches to the active `Camera`. Every frame, it synchronizes `Camera.position` and `Camera.forward`/`Camera.up` vectors to `AudioContext.listener`.

**[`SpatialAudioComponent`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/audio/components/SpatialAudioComponent.ts)**: Extends `Component` and attaches to any `Entity`. It creates and positions a Web Audio `PannerNode` with HRTF binaural panning and exponential/inverse distance rolloff models.

blocks.text: E. WebGPU Audio-Reactivity (AudioAnalyzer.ts)
`AudioAnalyzer` taps into the audio graph with an `AnalyserNode`:

items: **Macro Bands**: Computes normalized `bass` (0–15%), `mid` (15–60%), `treble` (60–100%), and overall `rms` energy values $[0.0 - 1.0]$.

**1D GPU Texture Streaming**: Allocates a 1D `r8unorm` `GPUTexture` with width equal to `frequencyBinCount`. Every frame, `analyzer.updateSpectrumTexture(device)` uploads FFT bins via `device.queue.writeTexture` for direct sampling in WGSL shaders.

blocks.text: F. Video Export Integration ([Recorder.ts](../src/engine/recorder/Recorder.ts))
When recording canvas output to MP4 or WebM:

items: `AudioManager` provides a `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`.
`LiveRecorder` connects an `AudioEncoder` (AAC for MP4, Opus for WebM) via `MediaStreamTrackProcessor`.
Audio chunks are muxed alongside video chunks into `mp4-muxer` and `webm-muxer`, exporting complete, synchronized video files.

5. Lifecycle & Clean Disposal
When scenes are reset (`scene.reset()`), seeked (`scene.seekTo()`), or destroyed (`scene.destroy()`):

items: **Seeking**: Active `AudioBufferSourceNode` instances are gracefully stopped, and new nodes are scheduled with exact fractional offsets.
**Pausing / Resuming**: Timeline tracking stops and resumes in sync with `scene.pause()` and `scene.resume()`.

**Destruction**: `scene.destroy()` automatically unregisters all lifecycle listeners, cleans up window/canvas unlock listeners, frees `GPUTexture` spectrum textures, and safely closes the `AudioContext`.
